The Smith & Wesson Model 1917 is a large-frame, double-action revolver developed in 1917. Chambered in .45 ACP and using half-moon clips for quick reloading, it was built on the sturdy N-frame and based on the Second Model Hand Ejector. Renowned for its accuracy, stopping power, and durability, the M1917 served in both World Wars and later became a respected and collectible civilian sidearm.

The Smith & Wesson Model 1917 is a large-frame, double-action revolver developed in 1917. Chambered in .45 ACP and using half-moon clips for quick reloading, it was built on the sturdy N-frame and based on the Second Model Hand Ejector. Renowned for its accuracy, stopping power, and durability, the M1917 served in both World Wars and later became a respected and collectible civilian sidearm.
 
 This Model 1917 has had its barrel shortened, its trigger and hammer re-machined, and its metal surfaces refinished, resulting in a small(ish), mean and loud lead dispenser.
